_about: Golden vectors of the rBFT handoff table, version 1 (docs/design/handoff-table.md). Written by gen_handoff_vectors.py, an independent second implementation of the layout; read by harness/test/test_handoff_vec.c. 'info' describes a table (hex fields are byte strings, ip_text is for humans), 'body' and 'table' are the exact bytes (hex). Keys are fixed fake patterns.

valid.name: typical_ipv4_nokey
valid.why: three IPv4 monitors, no key, DHCP NIC, fsid known, crc mode

valid.name: typical_ipv4_key_aes256k
valid.why: the same with the key in the table (aes256k, 32 bytes) and the image opened read-only

valid.name: key_aes_legacy_16
valid.why: legacy aes key, 16 bytes, secure-first mode

valid.name: eight_ipv6_monitors
valid.why: eight IPv6 monitors, IPv6 NIC with a VLAN, secure required, snapshot and image id

valid.name: all_flags_key_64
valid.why: every flag, a 64-byte key, VLAN 4094, static IPv4, mode secure-only

valid.name: minimal_no_auth
valid.why: no authentication, no entity, one monitor, NIC unknown

valid.name: utf8_names
valid.why: names are UTF-8: two-byte and three-byte sequences

valid.name: max_size_1024
valid.why: the whole table is exactly 1,024 bytes: 255-byte entity and image, 135-byte pool, 8 monitors, 64-byte key

refuse_decode.name: acpi_checksum_oem_changed
refuse_decode.why: an OEM byte changed without fixing the checksum (what iPXE does before it fixes it)

refuse_decode.name: acpi_length_too_small
refuse_decode.why: length field smaller than the header plus the fixed part

refuse_decode.name: acpi_length_beyond_buffer
refuse_decode.why: the buffer is one byte shorter than the length field says

refuse_decode.name: msgr_mode_5
refuse_decode.why: msgr_mode 5 (stock) is not a table value

refuse_decode.name: mon_count_beyond_area
refuse_decode.why: mon_count 8 but only 3 records are there

refuse_decode.name: key_len_beyond_area
refuse_decode.why: key_len 33 where 32 key bytes are left

refuse_decode.name: key_len_31_aes256k
refuse_decode.why: aes256k key_len 31 (the core accepts 32 and more), key bytes shortened to match

refuse_decode.name: key_len_15_aes
refuse_decode.why: aes key_len 15 (the core accepts 16 and more), key bytes shortened to match

refuse_decode.name: key_flag_without_offset
refuse_decode.why: key flag set, key offset absent

refuse_decode.name: key_offset_without_flag
refuse_decode.why: key offset present, key flag clear

refuse_decode.name: key_fields_without_flag
refuse_decode.why: key_type and key_len set, key flag clear

refuse_decode.name: key_with_auth_none
refuse_decode.why: key flag set with auth none

refuse_decode.name: fsid_without_flag
refuse_decode.why: fsid not zero, fsid flag clear

refuse_decode.name: nic_ipv4_tail_not_zero
refuse_decode.why: IPv4 address with a non-zero byte beyond the fourth

refuse_decode.name: mon_reserved_not_zero
refuse_decode.why: reserved byte of a monitor record not zero

refuse_decode.name: mon_ipv4_tail_not_zero
refuse_decode.why: IPv4 monitor with a non-zero byte beyond the fourth

refuse_decode.name: offset_entity_out_of_range
refuse_decode.why: entity offset beyond the variable area

refuse_decode.name: offset_pool_out_of_range
refuse_decode.why: pool offset beyond the variable area

refuse_decode.name: offset_image_out_of_range
refuse_decode.why: image offset beyond the variable area

refuse_decode.name: offset_mons_out_of_range
refuse_decode.why: monitor offset beyond the variable area

refuse_decode.name: offset_key_out_of_range
refuse_decode.why: key offset beyond the variable area

refuse_decode.name: string_unterminated
refuse_decode.why: snapshot offset points at the last two bytes of the area, which hold no NUL

refuse_decode.name: string_256_bytes
refuse_decode.why: the pool is 256 bytes long (the maximum is 255)

refuse_decode.name: string_present_but_empty
refuse_decode.why: image id present as an empty string (absent is the way to say none)

refuse_decode.name: layout_gap_between_strings
refuse_decode.why: a stray byte between the entity and the pool, offsets adjusted

refuse_decode.name: layout_strings_swapped
refuse_decode.why: entity and pool in the wrong order (offsets consistent)

refuse_decode.name: layout_overlap
refuse_decode.why: the pool offset points into the entity string

refuse_decode.name: layout_key_overlaps_monitors
refuse_decode.why: the key offset points into the monitor records

refuse_encode.name: pool_136_over_1024
refuse_encode.why: the maximum table with a 136-byte pool: 1,025 bytes

refuse_encode.name: key_not_allowed_without_flag
refuse_encode.why: key bytes given but the key flag clear: refused, not dropped

refuse_encode.name: static_without_family
refuse_encode.why: static NIC flag with an unknown family
